<item>
  <title>"Proof that there are infinitely many prime numbers:

Assume there are finitely many primes:
p1, p2, p3, ..., pn

Consider the number:
N = p1 * p2 * p3 * ... * pn + 1

Now, for every prime pi:
N mod pi = 1

Thus, N is not divisible by any of the known primes.

Therefore, either:
1) N is itself prime, or
2) N has a prime factor not in the list

In both cases, a new prime exists.

Contradiction.

⇒ There are infinitely many prime numbers." — euklid</title>
  <link>https://ImDuck42.github.io/Quotipedia/#quote/mmx77xrq-6z0c71570423</link>
  <guid isPermaLink="true">https://ImDuck42.github.io/Quotipedia/#quote/mmx77xrq-6z0c71570423</guid>
  <pubDate>Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:18:52 GMT</pubDate>
  <author>bob</author>
  <description>Proof that there are infinitely many prime numbers:

Assume there are finitely many primes:
p1, p2, p3, ..., pn

Consider the number:
N = p1 * p2 * p3 * ... * pn + 1

Now, for every prime pi:
N mod pi = 1

Thus, N is not divisible by any of the known primes.

Therefore, either:
1) N is itself prime, or
2) N has a prime factor not in the list

In both cases, a new prime exists.

Contradiction.

⇒ There are infinitely many prime numbers.</description>
